title: The Monkey and the Camel
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: At a gathering of all the beasts the Monkey gave an exhibition of dancing and entertained the company vastly. There was great applause at the finish, which excited the envy of the Camel and made him desire to win the favour of the assembly by the same means. So he got up from his place and began dancing, but he cut such a ridiculous figure as he plunged about, and made such a grotesque exhibition of his ungainly person, that the beasts all fell upon him with ridicule and drove him away.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Monkey do at the gathering of the beasts?
options: Gave an exhibition of dancing
Told a series of jokes
Sang a long song
Performed acrobatic tricks on a rope

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the company respond to the Monkey's dancing?
options: There was great applause at the finish
They demanded he dance again immediately
They ignored him and talked among themselves
They asked him to teach them his steps

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what feeling did the applause excite in the Camel?
options: Envy
Amusement
Sympathy
Boredom

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Camel desire to do after seeing the applause?
options: Win the favour of the assembly by the same means
Challenge the Monkey to a contest of strength
Ask the Monkey to teach him to dance in private
Leave the gathering before his turn came

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Camel do after he got up from his place?
options: Began dancing
Sang a song of his own
Applauded the Monkey once more
Challenged the Monkey to a race

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the beasts respond to the Camel's dancing?
options: They fell upon him with ridicule and drove him away
They applauded even louder than before
They asked him to dance a second time
They quietly left the gathering

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the beasts react so differently to the Camel's dancing than to the Monkey's?
options: The Camel's large, ungainly body was ill-suited to dancing, unlike the nimble Monkey's
The beasts had grown tired of dancing by the time the Camel performed
The Camel danced for a much longer time than the Monkey had
The beasts disliked the Camel personally, regardless of his performance

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Envying another's success and trying to copy it without regard for one's own nature invites ridicule
Camels are more talented performers than monkeys realize
Applause from a crowd is never a reliable sign of true skill
Every animal at a gathering deserves a turn to perform

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did this dancing take place?
options: At a gathering of all the beasts
At the Camel's home
In a marketplace
Beside a river

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how is the Camel's dancing figure described?
options: A ridiculous figure
A graceful figure
A powerful figure
An unnoticed figure

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kind of exhibition did the Camel's person make as he danced?
options: A grotesque exhibition of his ungainly person
A modest and dignified exhibition
An exhibition that impressed even the Monkey
An exhibition that no one noticed at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what mistake did the Camel make in trying to win the same praise as the Monkey?
options: He assumed the same act that suited the Monkey would suit him too
He waited too long before beginning his performance
He asked the Monkey for permission before dancing
He performed the exact same dance as the Monkey

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "ungainly" mean in "his ungainly person"?
options: Awkward and lacking grace
Extremely swift and light
Small and delicate
Beautifully proportioned

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Monkey's dancing is applauded, so the envious Camel tries the same and is driven away for his ridiculous attempt
The Camel outdances the Monkey and wins the crowd's favour
The Monkey and Camel dance together and both are applauded equally
The beasts refuse to let either the Monkey or the Camel perform
